topic: Research: Claude Fable 5 vs Claude Opus 4.8 vs DeepSeek V4 Pro: Which to Use (2026)

key_points: Anthropic positions Claude Fable 5 as the public, safeguarded version of the Mythos-class model family, with Mythos 5 reserved for trusted cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers.
Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.
Anthropic says Mythos-class models sit above Opus in capability and can work autonomously longer than prior Claude models.
Claude Fable 5 became generally available on June 9, 2026 across the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.
Claude Mythos 5 is limited to approved Project Glasswing customers, while Fable 5 offers the same capabilities with added safeguards.
Fable 5 and Mythos 5 require 30-day data retention, are not available under zero data retention, use adaptive thinking by default, and never return raw chain-of-thought content.
Claude Opus 4.8 is marketed as a premium model for serious coding, knowledge work, agentic workflows, and high-stakes enterprise tasks.
Anthropic emphasizes Opus 4.8's improved honesty, better uncertainty flagging, stronger tool calling, and lower rates of misaligned behavior than Opus 4.7.
Opus 4.8 launched with Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code, letting Claude plan large tasks and run many parallel subagents in a session.
DeepSeek V4 Preview launched with DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, both supporting one-million-token context windows.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro is described as a 1.6T-total-parameter, 49B-active-parameter model with performance rivaling top closed-source models.
DeepSeek presents V4 as a cost-effective long-context option available through chat.deepseek.com and API access.
Frames Opus 4.8 as the stronger production bug-fixing model and DeepSeek V4 Pro as the cost/value and algorithmic-coding winner.
Claims Opus 4.8 leads DeepSeek V4 Pro on SWE-bench Pro by 69.2% to 55.4%, while DeepSeek leads on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and LiveCodeBench.
Highlights a major price contrast: Opus 4.8 at $25 per million output tokens versus DeepSeek V4 Pro at $0.87 per million output tokens.

stats.fact: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 launched on June 9, 2026; Fable 5 was initially generally available on Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.
Anthropic priced Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

On June 12, 2026, Anthropic suspended access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 after a U.S. government export-control directive covering foreign nationals; access to other Anthropic models was not affected.
Anthropic's Claude release notes state that access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 was suspended on June 12, 2026 and that the company aims to return access as quickly as possible.
Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 require 30-day data retention and are not available under zero data retention.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro is listed by DeepSeek as 1.6T total parameters with 49B active parameters and one-million-token context support.
Hugging Face's DeepSeek-V4-Pro model card describes V4-Pro as a Mixture-of-Experts model with 1.6T parameters, 49B activated parameters, and one-million-token context length.
DataCamp reports Claude Fable 5 at 80.3% on SWE-bench Pro versus Claude Opus 4.8 at 69.2%, and 64.5% on Humanity's Last Exam with tools versus 57.9% for Opus 4.8.
Vals AI reports Claude Fable 5 at 95.0% on SWE-bench Verified and Claude Opus 4.8 at 88.6%.

CodingFleet reports Claude Opus 4.8 at 69.2% on SWE-bench Pro and DeepSeek V4 Pro at 55.4%, while DeepSeek V4 Pro leads on Terminal-Bench 2.0, 67.9% versus 65.4%, and LiveCodeBench, 93.5% versus 88.8%.
CodingFleet reports Opus 4.8 output pricing at $25 per million tokens and DeepSeek V4 Pro at $0.87 per million output tokens, a 28.7x price gap.
TechCrunch reported early Fable 5 data showing at least 95% of Fable sessions running entirely on Fable responses, with high-risk categories falling back to Opus 4.8.

angles: Lead with the June 2026 availability shock: Fable 5 may be the strongest model on paper, but the immediate buying question is whether your team can access it after the June 12 suspension.

Use a routing framework instead of a single winner: Fable 5 for frontier long-horizon work when available, Opus 4.8 for reliable Anthropic production workflows, DeepSeek V4 Pro for open-weight, long-context, high-volume, or data-sovereignty needs.

Make the comparison practical by separating benchmark categories: real-code bug fixing, algorithmic coding, browser/computer-use agents, long-context repository analysis, compliance, and cost at scale.

Call out the compliance inversion: Fable 5 is a closed frontier model with mandatory retention and geopolitical availability risk, while DeepSeek V4 Pro is open-weight but may raise procurement, security, or China-origin review questions in some enterprises.

Explain fallback architecture: teams using Fable 5 should design automatic fallback to Opus 4.8 or another model because Fable refusals, retention requirements, and regulatory suspension can interrupt workflows.
Position Opus 4.8 as the conservative default for U.S. enterprise teams that want Anthropic quality without Mythos-class uncertainty.

Emphasize that DeepSeek V4 Pro's one-million-token context and low output price make it compelling for repeated codebase scans, synthetic data generation, retrieval-heavy workflows, and self-hosted environments.

Avoid benchmark absolutism: many cited scores come from vendor pages, model cards, or niche benchmark sites, so the article should recommend testing on the reader's own tasks before migrating production workloads.
